relationships.subject: THC
relationships.evidence_quote: The activation of cannabinoid CB1 receptors (CB1R) by Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main component of Cannabis sativa, induces analgesia.

relationships.subject: peptide 17
relationships.evidence_quote: the memory impairment produced by THC (3 mg/kg, IP) was suppressed only when coadministered with 17 (20 mg/kg, IV)

relationships.subject: peptide 17
relationships.evidence_quote: interfering peptides 1 and 3 successfully blocked key biochemical signatures (cross-antagonism and negative cross-talk) of the CB1R–5HT2AR heteromer

key_findings: An orally active 16-residue D-amino acid peptide (17) that crosses the BBB disrupts the CB1R-5HT2AR heteromer and abolishes THC-induced memory impairment in mice while preserving THC analgesia.
